'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**Former [[Tigray Region]] president and fugitive [[Debretsion Gebremichael]] speaks out for the first time since going into hiding following the [[Mekelle offensive (2020)|fall of Mekelle]] to [[Ethiopian National Defense Force|federal forces]] in November 2020, saying "They [the federal government] have temporary military dominance", and "we are engaged in extended resistance". His current whereabouts are unknown. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ethiopia-conflict/fugitive-ex-leader-of-ethiopias-tigray-region-vows-extended-resistance-idUSKBN2A00BW?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**A [[suicide bomber]] [[detonation|blows himself up]] outside the Afrik Hotel in [[Mogadishu]], [[Somalia]], while gunmen storm the hotel and open fire. Five people are killed in the [[al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] attack, including a former [[Somali Armed Forces|military]] general; ten civilians are wounded. The three other attackers are shot dead during a gun battle with security forces. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-55879679 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Israel]] reports its first reinfection case of the 501.V2 variant in a 57-year-old man who recently travelled to [[Turkey]] and who previously recovered from COVID-19. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israeli-who-recovered-from-covid-19-reinfected-with-south-african-strain/ (''Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon]]
****[[Lebanon]] surpasses 300,000 cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [http://www.dailystar.com.lb/News/Lebanon-News/2021/Jan-31/516874-lebanon-surpasses-300000-covid-19-cases.ashx (''The Daily Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] agrees to transfer 5,000 doses of [[COVID-19 vaccine]] to the [[Palestinians]] to immunize frontline medical workers. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-55879337 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] extends its [[social distancing]] restrictions for another two weeks amid concern around the upcoming [[Chinese New Year|Lunar New Year]] holidays and an increase in the number of cases. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-01-31/south-korea-extends-social-distance-measures-after-resurgence (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant in a 25-year-old man from [[South Africa]] who travelled to [[Hanoi]] on December 19 and tested positive for COVID-19 four days later while in quarantine. [https://thewest.com.au/news/health/vietnam-gets-first-s-african-covid-case-ng-s-2047562 (AAP via ''The West Australian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The number of hospitalized [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] patients in [[France]] reaches 27,613, the most since December 1. [https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-france-idUKKBN2A00PF (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****[[List of Ministers of Education of the Netherlands|Minister for Primary Education]] [[Arie Slob]] announces that primary schools and daycare centres will reopen on February 8, but secondary schools and after-school clubs will remain closed. [https://www.dutchnews.nl/news/2021/01/primary-schools-daycare-will-reopen-on-february-8-minister-confirms/ (Dutch News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[Captain Tom]], a [[British Army]] [[World War II]] veteran who raised millions of pounds for charity during the [[pandemic]], is hospitalized after testing positive for COVID-19. He has not yet received a COVID-19 vaccine. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/100-year-old-vet-who-raised-millions-uk-health-service-n1256302 (NBC News)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-beds-bucks-herts-55895576 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Western Australia]] [[Premier of Western Australia|Premier]] [[Mark McGowan]] announces a five-day [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in the [[Perth metropolitan region|Perth metropolitan]], [[Peel (Western Australia)|Peel]], and [[South West (Western Australia)|South West]] regions, beginning at 6:00 p.m. [[Time in Australia|AWST]], after a quarantine hotel security guard tests positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], possibly of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]]. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/wa-records-first-locally-acquired-covid19-case-in-almost-10-months-coronavirus-wa/c1393ff5-bc29-492b-b4de-61eb4e4065bb (9 News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cuba]]
***[[Cuba]] reports a record 1,012 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 26,686. [https://www.plenglish.com/index.php?o=rn&id=63998&SEO=cuba-reports-record-of-1012-new-covid-19-cases (Presna Latina)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
***[[Egypt]] receives its first shipment of 50,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|AstraZeneca vaccine]] from [[India]]. [http://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/1/64/400028/Egypt/Politics-/UPDATE--Egypt-receives-first-batch-of-AstraZeneca-.aspx (Ahram Online)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**[[2021 Russian protests]], aftermath of the [[poisoning of Alexei Navalny]]
***[[United States Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] condemns [[Russia]]n authorities for using "harsh tactics" in protests that broke out following the arrest of [[Alexei Navalny]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/blinken-condemns-harsh-tactics-thousands-detained-navalny-protests-russia-n1256288 (NBC News)]
*[[Hong Kong–United Kingdom relations]], [[immigration to the United Kingdom]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] formally launches a visa scheme allowing all [[Hong Kong]] residents with [[British National (Overseas) passport]]s (BNO), and their "immediate dependents", to fast-track their UK citizenship. At least 300,000 people are expected to apply. In response, the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China]] says that it will "no longer recognise" BNO passports as legal travel documents. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55847572 (BBC News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**Police in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]] announce that they have arrested more than 400 people in order to prevent a banned demonstration against anti-[[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] measures. [https://www.dw.com/en/coronavirus-digest-brussels-police-detain-hundreds-of-protesters/a-56394523 (DW)]
*[[2021 Russian protests]]
**More than 5,000 people are detained by police at nationwide protests calling for the release of jailed opposition leader [[Alexei Navalny]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-55876033 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Vietnam]]
**[[Nguyễn Phú Trọng]] is re-elected as [[General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam]] for a third five-year term as top leader in [[Vietnam]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-vietnam-politics-congress/vietnam-ruling-communist-party-chief-trong-re-elected-for-third-term-idUSKBN2A005T (Reuters)]
*[[Shirlene Ostrov]] resigns as chairwoman of the [[Hawaii Republican Party]] following a series of tweets posted by vice chairman [[Edwin Boyette]] on the party's [[Twitter]] account defending people who supported the [[QAnon]] conspiracy theory. Additionally, Boyette resigned on January 24th after the tweets were posted the day before. [https://apnews.com/article/hawaii-gop-chair-resigns-qanon-tweets-587b54cd8b1accd01ef907324df6d6e5 (AP)]
